Classification: High Clan

Called the Graverobbers, the Cappadocians are obsessed with death and undeath, particularly with what remains once the soul departs the body. Founded by Cappadocius, who is believed to have originated in Anatolia or Armenia, the clan's spiritual center is the temple at Erciyes, where fragments of the Book of Nod were reputedly collected. Cappadocians gather in monastic libraries, graveyards, catacombs, temples and universities to disseminate what they learn. The clan has recently taken great interest in a Venetian merchant family, the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni}, who have been making inroads into necromantic study.

Disciplines: Auspex, Fortitude, Mortis

Advantage: As scholars first and foremost, all Cappadocians gain one free Trait of Health, Learning or Occult Influence, and an associated Ability of Academics, Medicine or Occult. Their reputation as scholars often admits them to nearly any library.

Disadvantage: Cappadocians are cursed to look like corpses — ghastly pallor and emaciated bodies — no matter how much blood they drink; they cannot induce a living appearance by spending blood, though blood may otherwise be spent normally. This worsens with age, and they suffer a one-Trait penalty on Social Challenges where their appearance is visible.

Organization: Less political than most High Clans, but valued by them for knowledge and contacts. Members act as royal tutors, advisors, or simply pursue research in seclusion, often for years at a stretch.

Suggested Viae: Heaven or Sin; the most spiritual (and morbid) follow the Path of Bones.
